# Feature: Choice Integrity

## 1. Feature Goal

**ID**: FEAT-038
**Source Plan**: `.spec-lite/plan_interaction_wave2_gaps.md`

A choice the interaction layer offers the model must be **distinguishable**, **receivable**, and **safe**. Today none of the three holds, and the same run pays for each of them.

**Distinguishable.** [`calendar-driver.ts:244-256`](../../../packages/core/src/widgets/date/calendar-driver.ts) filters the grid to `cells.filter((cell) => cell.derivedDate === date)` and, on more than one hit, reports `WIDGET_AMBIGUOUS_CHOICE/several-matched-equally` with `offered: matches.map((cell) => \`${cell.monthLabel}: ${cell.name}\`)`. When two distinct DOM cells carry the same accessible name, that array holds the same string twice, and [`fill/types.ts:250-256`](../../../packages/core/src/fill/types.ts) tells the model to _"Re-issue this call with one of those strings exactly as written."_ There is no string it can send. The cells are genuinely different elements — `calendar-grid.ts:400,416`dedupes by DOM`path`before pushing — and they are fully separable **structurally**:`CalendarCell` (`calendar-grid.ts:8-21`) carries `path`, `selected`, `disabled`, and `group`. The driver discards all of it and asks for a decision that cannot be made.

**Receivable.** `selectByOfferedLabel` exists exactly once, at [`combobox-driver.ts:281`](../../../packages/core/src/widgets/combobox/combobox-driver.ts), and three templates declare it as their capability — including the one the **calendar** emits. FEAT-032's gate (`failure-causes.spec.ts:78-88`) asserts only `typeof exported[template.capability] === 'function'`: a package export of that _name_. It cannot see that the family which emitted the advice has no route to it. In the motivating run the agent obeyed the hint twice, the date value fell through to the typeahead path, and both calls ended in `WIDGET_TARGET_UNREACHABLE` after 6.4 s and 5.6 s.

**Safe.** [`combobox-driver.ts:450`](../../../packages/core/src/widgets/combobox/combobox-driver.ts) maps `reaction.candidates` straight into `offered`, and `collectCandidates` selects on `'[role="option"],button,a[href],[role="menuitem"],li[onclick],li[tabindex]'` (`option/candidates.ts:76-77`) — bare `button` included. Against an open date panel that produced `offered: ["Round trip","One way","Reset","Previous","Next","Done. Search for one-way flights, …"]` for a **return date** field, attached to a hint saying to re-issue with one of them exactly as written. Following that advice with `"One way"` or `"Reset"` destroys the round-trip search the user asked for. `PROTECTED_ACTION_RE` correctly does not match those strings; the defect is not the lexicon, it is that container **chrome** is offered as **choices** at all.

**After this feature.** An `offered` list is treated as what it demonstrably is — a menu the agent will pick from, not diagnostic output:

- Indistinguishable candidates are resolved structurally, inside the driver's already-resolved container, and the substitution is disclosed in the result and counted in the ledger. `WIDGET_AMBIGUOUS_CHOICE` is reported **only** when the survivors differ in a way the model can act on.
- The date family exports and routes a real offered-label receiver, and the capability gate becomes a mapping from `(surface, family)` to the receiver that family exports — so a family emitting advice it cannot honor is a test failure, not a run-time dead end.
- Candidates are scoped by option role where the container declares one, vetoed by `PROTECTED_ACTION_RE`, and `offered` is advertised only where the container has option semantics at all. Where it has none, the hint stops naming strings and says so.

Three new protocol fixtures (`indistinguishable-choices`, `chrome-in-overlay`, `offered-label-roundtrip-date`) take the two-tier gauntlet from **17 to 20** and make the gate able to see all three defects, which the existing `ambiguous-suggestions` fixture structurally cannot: in it the labels differ, the emitting family owns the receiver, and the container holds nothing but options.

### Non-negotiable constraints

- **No website-specific automation logic** (memory → General; plan §8). Every rule below reads container scope, ARIA role, enabled/visible state, and document order. A site name may appear only as provenance in a fixture's leading HTML comment — never in the fixture body and never under `packages/*/src`, enforced by `widget-regressions.spec.ts:157` and `boundary-rules.spec.ts:70`.
- **A structural tie-break clicks a control the model did not choose.** Per plan §6 it is permitted **only** when (i) every surviving candidate is indistinguishable to the model, (ii) the choice is inside the driver's already-resolved container, and (iii) the substitution is disclosed in the result. Where candidates differ in any model-visible way, the choice stays the agent's.
- **`packages/core` must never import `@yantra/agent`** (memory → Project Structure). Everything in this feature is core-internal; `PROTECTED_ACTION_RE` already lives at `packages/core/src/interaction/protected-actions.ts`. The one agent-side edit is tool-description prose.
- **Advice may only name an engineered capability** (memory → Coding Standards). This feature is the mechanical enforcement FEAT-032 intended, moved from _"a function of this name is exported"_ to _"the family that emits this can receive it"_.
- **Exactly one implementation of each shared rule.** `boundary-rules.spec.ts:87` forbids `query-plan.ts` from importing anything outside `./`, and `:103` pins `candidates.ts` to the literal `return rankAgainstRequested(candidates, requested);`. The tie-break therefore lives in `interaction/` and is reached from inside `rankAgainstRequested`, never restated in a driver.
- **No new stable error code.** `message-catalog.spec.ts:FROZEN_STABLE_CODES` stays byte-identical; this feature adds one new **cause** under an existing code.
- **Existing fixtures and green tests stay green.** The tests whose expectations legitimately change are enumerated in §6 and named per task.

### Accepted follow-on (plan §7, deliberate)

FEAT-038's new ledger evidence — the substitution count and position — is written into the **legacy** `AttemptRecord.detail` projection now, and moves to `RungVerdict` evidence in **FEAT-040**. This is one small, named rewrite accepted by the plan's ordering. **Do not implement FEAT-040's work here**: `toLegacyLedger`, `queryRecord`, and `renumber` stay exactly as they are.

### Explicitly out of scope

FEAT-039's `covers` disclosure on `browser_fill_form`; FEAT-040's shared run state, `toWireLedger` on the fill path, and the `process.cwd()` fixture path in `recovery-characterization.spec.ts` (touched here only to bump a census number); anything FEAT-031/032/033/034/037 shipped.

## 2. Data Model (Granular)

> `.spec-lite/data_model.md` does **not** exist, and plan §3 states plainly that **every change is in existing files** with no additions. There are therefore **no tables, no columns, no migrations, no indexes, and no foreign keys in this feature**. Everything below is a **TypeScript contract shape** inside `packages/core` plus the one serialized projection those shapes reach — `details.offered`, `details.attempted[].detail`, and `FillSuccess.substitution` in `tool-calls.jsonl`. The plan gives the rules; the granular shapes are designed here.

### Entities & Attributes

**`ChoiceTieBreakRung`** — the rung of the structural ladder that narrowed a tie. A closed union of **structural strings only**, so it is safe to log verbatim (same reasoning as FEAT-033's `ObstructionKind` and FEAT-034's `EntryDecision.unmet`).

`'within-container' | 'enabled-and-visible' | 'page-selected' | 'document-order'`.

Deliberately **not** `resolution.ts`'s `TieBreakRung`, which answers a different question — _which live node is the control the caller already identified_ — and is documented as such at `resolution.ts:38-48`. This union answers _which of several offers the model cannot tell apart_. Keeping them separate is what stops one from silently acquiring the other's safety boundary.

**`StructuralChoice`** — the minimum a candidate must expose to be tie-broken. Structural only; nothing here is a value judgement.

- `path` (`readonly number[]`) — NOT NULL. The serializable element-path already minted by `collectCandidates` and `readCalendarGrid`. Document order is `path` lexicographic order; container membership is a path-prefix test. This is the whole reason the helper needs no port.
- `disabled` (`boolean`, optional) — absent means "not known to be disabled".
- `hidden` (`boolean`, optional) — absent means "not known to be hidden". Both producers already filter on visibility, so this is a declared slot rather than a new read.
- `selected` (`boolean`, optional) — the page's own `aria-selected`/`aria-checked` mark. `CalendarCell.selected` already carries it (`calendar-grid.ts:381-383`); `WidgetCandidate` gains it in TASK-004.

**`ChoiceSubstitution`** — what was taken on the model's behalf, and the only thing that makes rule 5 permissible.

- `indistinguishable` (`number`) — NOT NULL, **≥ 2**. How many survivors shared one model-visible label.
- `position` (`number`) — NOT NULL, 1-based document-order position taken. Always `1` today; declared as a number so the ledger says which one rather than implying there was only one rule.
- `tieBreak` (`readonly ChoiceTieBreakRung[]`) — NOT NULL, may be empty. Which rungs actually narrowed the pool, in order applied.
- `label` (`string`) — NOT NULL. The shared model-visible label. **Page-derived**: it reaches the model-visible note and passes the same sanitizer as any other observation field, and it is **never** written to the ledger (plan §10 — only the count is).

**`ChoiceOutcome<T>`** — a four-arm discriminated union. The arms are the point: "one obvious answer", "one answer taken on your behalf", and "your choice to make" are three different facts and must not share a shape.

- `{ kind: 'unique'; choice: T; tieBreak }` — rungs 1–3 left exactly one survivor. **No substitution**: nothing was taken on the model's behalf.
- `{ kind: 'substituted'; choice: T; substitution: ChoiceSubstitution }` — rule 5 fired. Every survivor carried an identical model-visible label; the first in document order was taken and the substitution is disclosed.
- `{ kind: 'ambiguous'; survivors: readonly T[] }` — rule 4. Survivors differ in a model-visible way; this is genuine ambiguity and the existing, correct behavior.
- `{ kind: 'none' }` — the input was empty. Callers keep their own not-found failures; the helper never invents one.

**`ResolveChoiceOptions<T>`** — how a caller projects its own candidate type onto the rule.

- `label` (`(choice: T) => string`) — NOT NULL. **Exactly the string this candidate would contribute to `offered`.** The calendar passes `` (cell) => `${cell.monthLabel}: ${cell.name}` ``; the ranker passes `(candidate) => candidate.name`. Passing the offered projection rather than a name is what makes the invariant literally _"the strings in `offered` are pairwise distinct"_.
- `containerPath` (`readonly number[]`, optional) — the driver's already-resolved container. Rung 1 filters to candidates whose `path` is prefixed by it. `readonly number[]` and not `WidgetContainer`, so `interaction/choice.ts` imports nothing from `widgets/` and `query-plan.ts` keeps its `./`-only import rule (`boundary-rules.spec.ts:87`).
- `normalize` (`(value: string) => string`, optional) — defaults to the shared `normalizeText`. Identity is compared normalized, never raw, so trailing-whitespace variants of one label are still indistinguishable.

**The ladder itself** (plan §7, "The tie-break rule, stated so it cannot become site logic"). Every rung **filters only when it leaves something behind**, exactly as `resolution.ts:narrow` already does, so the ladder can never invent a winner from an empty set:

| #   | Rung                  | Rule                                                                                                              |
| --- | --------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1   | `within-container`    | Prefer candidates whose `path` is prefixed by `containerPath`. Skipped when no container path was supplied.       |
| 2   | `enabled-and-visible` | Prefer `disabled !== true && hidden !== true`.                                                                    |
| 3   | `page-selected`       | Prefer `selected === true`.                                                                                       |
| 4   | —                     | More than one survivor with **differing** normalized labels → `ambiguous`. Unchanged, correct behavior.           |
| 5   | `document-order`      | More than one survivor with **identical** normalized labels → take the `path`-lexicographic first, `substituted`. |

Rule 5 is the whole change. Rules 1–4 are existing behavior made explicit so the ordering is testable. **No step consults a host, a URL, or a class name.**

**`WidgetCandidate`** (`option/candidates.ts:11-17`) — extended, not replaced:

- `selected` (`boolean`, optional) — read from `aria-selected === 'true' || aria-checked === 'true'` in the same page-context pass that already computes `disabled`. Optional so `calendar-driver.ts:273`'s hand-built candidate literal keeps compiling unchanged.

**`WidgetChoiceSet`** — the new return of `collectChoices`, and the structural answer to G3. It exists because _"what is clickable inside this container"_ and _"what this container offers as choices"_ are two different questions, and conflating them is precisely the defect.

- `choices` (`readonly WidgetCandidate[]`) — NOT NULL. What may be ranked, offered, and clicked.
- `semantics` (`'declared' | 'none'`) — NOT NULL. `'declared'` when the container carries an explicit option role (`[role="option"]`, `[role="menuitem"]`, `[role="treeitem"]` descendants) **or** declares a list role itself (`listbox`, `menu`, `menubar`, `tree`). `'none'` otherwise — a `role="dialog"` calendar panel is `'none'`.
- `scopedOut` (`number`) — NOT NULL. How many structurally-eligible controls option-role scoping removed. A **count**, never the names.
- `vetoed` (`number`) — NOT NULL. How many `PROTECTED_ACTION_RE` removed. A **count**, never the names.

Eligibility, in order:

1. If the container exposes explicit option-role descendants → `choices` are exactly those; every other control is chrome and is dropped (`scopedOut`).
2. Otherwise → today's `primarySelector` / named-children behavior, unchanged. **This is what keeps the existing button-based fixtures green**, and every option-bearing protocol fixture in the tree today uses `role="option"`.
3. In **both** tiers, a candidate whose name matches `PROTECTED_ACTION_RE` is removed entirely (`vetoed`) — never offered, never ranked, never clicked. This mirrors the obstruction protocol's clearance veto, which is a refusal to _press_, not merely to advertise.

`collectCandidates` keeps its current signature and semantics for `fill/dismiss.ts:uniqueCommitControl`, which is looking for a **release** control (`/^(done|apply|ok|save|close)$/i`) and not a choice. Scoping that call would break widget dismissal in exactly the mixed containers this feature adds a fixture for.

**Offered advertising rule.** Two rules, deliberately kept separate.

- **(a) Contents — everywhere.** `offered` carries the scoped-and-vetoed `choices` and nothing else, on success and on failure alike. This is what removes chrome and protected-action controls from every list the model ever sees.
- **(b) Withholding — the two named failure causes only.** On `WIDGET_TARGET_UNREACHABLE/no-suggestion-matched` and `.../value-not-offered` (the two surfaces plan §5 names), a container whose `semantics` is `'none'` carries **no `offered` key at all** and reports the new `no-options-offered` cause below, whose hint names no strings.

Success payloads are outside (b): a container with no ARIA list semantics that nonetheless commits a choice still reports what it offered, so `resolutionFor`'s `single_offered_match` / `selected_from_offered` split (`engine.ts:769-770`) is unchanged and no existing success note moves. `WIDGET_AMBIGUOUS_CHOICE` is also outside (b): after the veto and the tie-break, a genuine tie among a container's own controls is a real choice belonging to the caller, and reporting it is correct.

**New `InteractionFailureCause` member** — `'no-options-offered'`, registered under `WIDGET_TARGET_UNREACHABLE`:

- `requiredDetails: []`, `capability: null` — advice that asks the caller to **observe**, not to retry, which is the documented condition for a null capability (`fill/types.ts:126-135`).
- Hint (single instruction, textually distinct from every sibling): _"The container that opened exposes no selectable options, so there is nothing here to name back. Re-observe and address the control that carries the value, or report the gap."_
- Added to `unreachableCause`'s pass-through set. **No new error code** — `FROZEN_STABLE_CODES` is untouched.

**`FailureTemplate.emittedBy`** (`readonly InteractionFamily[]`, optional) — which interaction families can produce this `(code, cause)` pair. Required **in practice** by a runtime invariant ("every template with a non-null capability declares a non-empty `emittedBy`") rather than by the type system, because memory records that `pnpm --filter <pkg> typecheck` does not cover `tests/` and a type-level guarantee living in a test file is imaginary.

Declared values, derived from the emitters verified in the working tree:

| Template                                            | `emittedBy`                           | Emitter sites                                                                                   |
| --------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `WIDGET_AMBIGUOUS_CHOICE/several-matched-equally`   | `['combobox','date','option','text']` | `combobox-driver.ts:568`, `calendar-driver.ts:248`, `listbox-driver.ts:79,117`, `engine.ts:880` |
| `WIDGET_TARGET_UNREACHABLE/no-suggestion-matched`   | `['combobox','text']`                 | `combobox-driver.ts:581`, `engine.ts:888`                                                       |
| `WIDGET_TARGET_UNREACHABLE/value-not-offered`       | `['option']`                          | `listbox-driver.ts:134`                                                                         |
| `WIDGET_TARGET_UNREACHABLE/driver-not-recognized`   | `['date','option']`                   | `engine.ts:driveFamilyPlan` probe arms (`probeEligible` excludes combobox)                      |
| `WIDGET_TARGET_UNREACHABLE/picker-did-not-open`     | `['date','option']`                   | same                                                                                            |
| `WIDGET_NOT_COMMITTED/keystrokes-landed-elsewhere`  | `['text','combobox']`                 | typing ladder's WHERE rung                                                                      |
| `OPTION_NOT_FOUND/option-not-found` (actionability) | `['option']`                          | `agent-controller.ts:1092-1096`                                                                 |

**`CapabilityReceiver`** — the replacement for the package-level export check (plan §12 item 3: _replaced, not supplemented_). Lives in a new `packages/core/src/interaction/capabilities.ts`.

- `surface` (`InteractionMessageSurface`) — NOT NULL.
- `family` (`InteractionFamily`) — NOT NULL. Reused unchanged from `escalation.ts:57`.
- `capability` (`string`) — NOT NULL. The capability name the template declares.
- `receiver` (`string`) — NOT NULL. Either a package-exported function name (`selectByOfferedLabel`) or `Class.method` (`AgentBrowserController.selectOption`), resolved by the gate in both forms.

`CAPABILITY_RECEIVERS` is the exported table; `receiverFor(surface, family, capability): string | null` is the lookup. **UNIQUE on `(surface, family, capability)`.** Declared rows:

| surface         | family     | capability             | receiver                              |
| --------------- | ---------- | ---------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| `fill`          | `combobox` | `selectByOfferedLabel` | `selectByOfferedLabel`                |
| `fill`          | `date`     | `selectByOfferedLabel` | `selectByOfferedCalendarLabel` (new)  |
| `fill`          | `option`   | `selectByOfferedLabel` | `rankAgainstRequested`                |
| `fill`          | `text`     | `selectByOfferedLabel` | `rankAgainstRequested`                |
| `fill`          | `date`     | `probeOpen`            | `probeOpen`                           |
| `fill`          | `option`   | `probeOpen`            | `probeOpen`                           |
| `fill`          | `text`     | `locateEditee`         | `locateEditee`                        |
| `fill`          | `combobox` | `locateEditee`         | `locateEditee`                        |
| `actionability` | `option`   | `selectByOfferedLabel` | `AgentBrowserController.selectOption` |

The receivers legitimately differ in kind, and that is the information the old check destroyed: `combobox` and `date` honor a re-issued label through a **dedicated entry path**, while `option` and `text` honor it through the **ordinary ranker's `exact` tier**. A family whose receiver is _nothing_ is the bug. `capabilityKind: 'tool'` rows (`browser_click` on the obstruction templates) keep their existing agent-side catalog check in `packages/agent/tests/runtime/message-catalog.spec.ts` and are out of this mapping.

**`UnreceivableAdviceError`** — thrown, not degraded, when a family emits a capability-bearing template it is not declared to emit or for which no receiver resolves. Same discipline as `DanglingHintError` (`fill/types.ts:381-401`): every reachable combination is enumerated by the invariant test, so a correct build cannot reach it. Carries `surface`, `code`, `cause`, `family`.

**`IndistinguishableOfferedError`** — thrown by `hintFor` when a template declaring `'offered'` in `requiredDetails` is handed an `offered` array with duplicate normalized members. This is the mechanical form of plan §11's target _"0 — structurally impossible"_: after the tie-break no producer can reach it, and the throw is what keeps that true. Carries `errorCode`, `failureCause`, and the duplicated label.

**`FillSuccess.substitution`** (`ChoiceSubstitution`, optional) — present only when rule 5 fired, in the same voice as the Wave 1 `editee` disclosure (`fill/types.ts:73-85`). Carried up from `WidgetSuccess.substitution` (also new and optional).

**New `success-note` template** — `FILL_SUCCESS_NOTE/structural_tie_break`, `requiredDetails: ['field','count','label']`, `capability: null`. Rendered into `FillSuccess.note`. `noteFor` gains one rule: a substitution always produces a note, including when `resolution === 'exact'` (which is what a tie-broken date is — the committed value _is_ what was asked for). `FillResolution` is **unchanged**; a structural tie-break does not change how `committed` relates to `requested`.

**Serialized projections touched** (no new key is ever always-empty, per plan §9):

| Key                          | Present when                          | Content                                                                                                     |
| ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `details.offered`            | `semantics === 'declared'`            | Page-derived labels, capped at `MAX_RANKED_OFFERED` (10), **pairwise distinct**                             |
| `substitution`               | rule 5 fired                          | `{ indistinguishable, position, tie_break, label }`                                                         |
| `note`                       | rule 5 fired, or resolution ≠ `exact` | One sentence; names the shared label                                                                        |
| `details.attempted[].detail` | rule 5 fired on that rung             | `resolved N indistinguishable choices, took position P via <rungs>` — **counts and structural tokens only** |

### Relationships

- One **`ResolveChoiceOptions.label`** projection 1:1 the string a candidate contributes to `offered`. This is the join that makes the catalog invariant checkable: distinctness of `ChoiceOutcome` survivors **is** distinctness of `offered`.
- One **`ChoiceOutcome{kind:'substituted'}`** 1:1 one `ChoiceSubstitution` 1:1 one `AttemptRecord.detail` clause and 1:1 one `FillSuccess.substitution`. A substitution that is not disclosed is a contract violation, asserted directly.
- One **`FailureTemplate`** with a non-null `capability` has N declared `emittedBy` families; each `(surface, family, capability)` triple 1:1 exactly one `CapabilityReceiver` row. A template arm with no row for a declared emitter is a test failure.
- One **`WidgetChoiceSet`** N:1 one `WidgetContainer`; `semantics` is a property of the container, `scopedOut` / `vetoed` of the pass.
- **`collectChoices`** (choices) and **`collectCandidates`** (anything clickable) are siblings over the same page read, related 1:1 by container. `fill/dismiss.ts` keeps the latter; the combobox, listbox, and virtual-list paths move to the former.

### Indexes & Constraints

- **UNIQUE `(surface, family, capability)` in `CAPABILITY_RECEIVERS`** — a duplicate makes "which receiver honors this" ambiguous. Asserted.
- **Totality: every capability-bearing template declares a non-empty `emittedBy`, and every declared emitter resolves a receiver.** Asserted at runtime, not at type level (memory → Testing: package `tsconfig.json` excludes `tests/`).
- **Emission integrity**: a family emitting a capability-bearing template it is not declared to emit throws `UnreceivableAdviceError`. This is what stops `emittedBy` from becoming decorative.
- **Pairwise-distinct `offered`**: enforced in `hintFor` for every template declaring `'offered'`, and asserted across the whole catalog.
- **Hint containment**: a rendered hint interpolates only members present in `details.offered` — asserted by rendering each `offered`-bearing template and matching every quoted run against the array.
- **Substitution disclosure**: `substitution.indistinguishable >= 2`, and a `substituted` outcome always produces both a `note` and a ledger `detail`. A resolved-but-undisclosed tie-break is a failing test.
- **Container containment**: a candidate whose `path` is not prefixed by `containerPath` is never the `choice` of a `substituted` outcome, whenever any in-container candidate exists. Property-tested.
- **Protected-action veto**: no member of `choices`, `offered`, or a `substituted` outcome matches `PROTECTED_ACTION_RE`. Asserted by name on the `chrome-in-overlay` fixture.
- **Exactly one tie-break implementation** in `packages/*/src`, alongside `boundary-rules.spec.ts`'s existing single-implementation rules; `candidates.ts` keeps its pinned one-line delegation.
- **`FROZEN_STABLE_CODES` unchanged** — one new cause, zero new codes.
- **Gauntlet census**: 16 protocol + 4 agent = **20**, stated as literals in three places so growing the gallery stays a deliberate edit.

## 4. Dependencies

- **FEAT-032 (Widget Gauntlet Harness)** — the two-tier registries, the counting port, the `followUp` mechanism, and the message catalog this feature extends. Implemented.
- **FEAT-034 (Recovery as Declarative Data)** — `InteractionFamily`, `runEscalationPlan`, `toLegacyLedger`, and the `AttemptRecord` projection the substitution evidence rides. Implemented. **Its phase-3 wire shape is FEAT-040's work, not this feature's.**
- **FEAT-037 (Shadow/Virtualized Widgets)** — `scanVirtualOptions` and `virtual-list.ts`, which move onto `collectChoices`. Implemented.
- **FEAT-033 (Obstruction Protocol)** — the precedent this feature follows for a structural veto on a control the engine may press. Implemented.
- **No dependency on FEAT-039 or FEAT-040.** Plan row order places both after this feature.

### TASK-001: The one structural tie-break, as a pure helper

- [ ] **Implementation**: Create `packages/core/src/interaction/choice.ts` with the §2 shapes and `resolveIndistinguishableChoice<T>(candidates, options): ChoiceOutcome<T>`. Implement the five-rung ladder from plan §7 exactly, with the `apply` discipline `resolution.ts:narrow` already uses — **a rung filters only when it leaves something behind and does not empty the pool**, and each rung that actually narrowed appends its name to `tieBreak`. Rung 1 is a `path`-prefix test against `options.containerPath`; rung 5 sorts survivors by `path` lexicographically and takes the first. Identity is compared through `options.normalize ?? normalizeText`. The module imports **nothing** from `widgets/` and holds no port, no clock, and no I/O. Export it from `interaction/index.ts`. Add the boundary rule to `packages/core/tests/boundary-rules.spec.ts`, following its existing "keeps candidate ranking to exactly one implementation" pattern: exactly one definition of `resolveIndistinguishableChoice` in `packages/*/src`, and `candidates.ts` still contains the literal `return rankAgainstRequested(candidates, requested);`. **No call sites in this task** — nothing in the suite moves.
- [ ] **Unit Tests**: `packages/core/tests/interaction/choice.spec.ts`. Cases: rungs apply in declared order and each records its name; a rung that would empty the pool is skipped and records nothing; a rung that narrows nothing records nothing; survivors with differing labels return `ambiguous` **whatever** their structural differences; survivors with identical labels return `substituted` with `indistinguishable === survivors.length` and `position === 1`; an empty input returns `none`; a single candidate returns `unique` with no substitution. Property tests with `fast-check` (already a dev dependency, used in `recovery-characterization.spec.ts`): over generated candidate sets, (a) a set containing **any** model-visible label difference among survivors never returns `substituted`; (b) a fully label-identical set always returns `substituted` and always picks the document-order minimum; (c) when at least one candidate sits inside `containerPath`, a candidate outside it is never the `choice`; (d) the outcome is invariant under input permutation.

## 6. Cross-Cutting Concerns

- **Auth**: N/A. No CLI flag, no preference, no consent decision, no new tool. Plan §5 states the CLI surface is unchanged.
- **Error Handling**: Stable error codes are **unchanged** and `FROZEN_STABLE_CODES` stays byte-identical; this feature adds exactly one cause, `no-options-offered`, under the existing `WIDGET_TARGET_UNREACHABLE`. Two new typed `Error` subclasses — `UnreceivableAdviceError` and `IndistinguishableOfferedError` — follow the `DanglingHintError` precedent: thrown rather than degraded, because both describe states a correct build cannot reach and both are enumerated by an invariant test. `classifyFailure`'s `details.reason === 'budget' | 'disabled'` override is untouched, and nothing is silently swallowed.
- **Logging**: The substitution rides the **existing** sanitized ledger as one `AttemptRecord` whose `detail` carries the count, the position taken, and the tie-break rung names — structural tokens only. **Filtered-out chrome is never logged as page text; only `scopedOut` and `vetoed` counts exist.** The shared label reaches the model-visible `note` and `substitution.label`, which pass the same sanitizer as every other observation field at the agent seam. No new sink, no new log level, structured Pino logging unchanged.
- **Security**: This is the feature's core concern, per plan §6 — _an offered choice is an instruction the agent will follow._ (i) Offered candidates are filtered to the container's own option semantics, never arbitrary focusable descendants. (ii) `PROTECTED_ACTION_RE` vetoes a candidate from being offered, ranked, **or** clicked, matching the obstruction protocol's clearance veto; it is necessary and not sufficient, which is why the structural rule carries the weight. (iii) A structural tie-break is a real action on the user's behalf and is permitted only under all three of plan §6's conditions — indistinguishable to the model, inside the driver's already-resolved container, disclosed in the result — each asserted directly. (iv) No offered string is ever synthesized; every one stays page-derived and sanitized. (v) The secret path is untouched: `allowEscalation: false` still builds a one-rung plan, still commits blind, and contributes no evidence, so no secret-derived value can reach an offered list, a substitution, or a ledger.
- **Dependency direction**: Every change is in `packages/core` except tool-description prose in `packages/agent`. `packages/core` imports nothing from `@yantra/agent`; `interaction/choice.ts` imports nothing from `widgets/`, keeping `query-plan.ts`'s `./`-only rule green. Both are already enforced by `boundary-rules.spec.ts`.
- **No website-specific logic**: every signal is container scope, ARIA role, enabled/visible state, page-marked selection, and document order. `isOfferedCalendarLabel` recognizes a string **this engine minted**, not a site's format. Fixture provenance stays in the leading HTML comment, enforced by `widget-regressions.spec.ts:157` across the whole core and agent source trees.
- **Backward compatibility**: No run directory is rewritten and no run-artifact reader changes. `substitution` and the new ledger `detail` are additive optional keys; a reader that ignores them sees exactly what it saw before. `FillResolution` is unchanged, so `docs/features/agentic-tasks.md`'s documented resolution set stays correct.
- **Testing**: Vitest, AAA behavior tests, injected clocks and ports, mocks only at external boundaries; suites tagged `@no-llm` and run on macOS, Windows, and Ubuntu. Fixture bytes are read through an explicit fatal UTF-8 decoder (`readUtf8`); on Windows, manual inspection uses `Get-Content -Encoding utf8`, never PowerShell 5.1's ANSI default. Targeted runs are `cd packages/<pkg> && npx vitest run <path>` — `pnpm --filter <pkg> test -- <pattern>` silently ignores the pattern, and `npx vitest run --root` breaks `recovery-characterization.spec.ts`'s `process.cwd()` fixture path. `e2e` resolves `@yantra/core` from built `dist/`, so `turbo run build` precedes any `e2e` verification.

### Tests whose expectations legitimately change

Everything else in the suite must pass **unedited**. These, and only these, change:

1. `packages/core/tests/fill/failure-causes.spec.ts:78-88` — the package-level `typeof exported[capability]` check is **replaced** by the per-`(surface, family)` gate (plan §12 item 3). TASK-006.
2. `packages/core/tests/interaction/message-catalog.spec.ts:71-76` — the same replacement for `capabilityKind: 'engine'`. TASK-006.
3. `packages/core/tests/interaction/widget-regressions.spec.ts:134` — protocol census `13` → `16`. TASK-008.
4. `packages/core/tests/interaction/recovery-characterization.spec.ts:20-22` — protocol census `13` → `16` and the `17-fixture` comment → `20`. TASK-008.
5. `e2e/widget-gauntlet.spec.ts:48,275-282` — `protocolFixtureCount` `13` → `16`, the combined gate `17` → `20`, and the test title. TASK-008.
6. `packages/core/tests/support/gauntlet.ts` — three new descriptors and two additive optional fields on `ExpectedOutcome`'s `commit` arm (`forbiddenOffered`, `substitution`). Existing descriptors are untouched.
